2025.source_note: Federal & FICA: IRS Rev. Proc. 2024-40 (standard deduction per OBBBA §70102) / SSA 2025. State schedules: each state's 2025 rates, deductions and exemptions by filing status (credits and local taxes not included). Estimate only — not tax advice; verify against official sources.

capital_gains.source_note: IRS Rev. Proc. 2024-40 §2.03 — long-term capital gains 0%/15%/20% breakpoints by filing status.

retirement_plans.source_note: IRS Notice 2024-80 — 401(k) elective deferral, age-50 and age-60–63 catch-ups, §415(c) annual additions and §401(a)(17) compensation limits, IRA limit and catch-up; HSA limits per Rev. Proc. 2024-25.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.note: Wage income untaxed (interest & dividends tax repealed effective 2025).

WA.name: Washington
WA.note: No tax on wage income (a separate capital-gains tax applies).

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.note: Flat 2.5%. Age/blind exemptions and the charitable addition to the deduction not modeled.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.note: Flat 4.4% of federal taxable income, so the federal standard deduction applies. The add-back of deductions above $12,000 ($16,000 joint) when AGI exceeds $300,000 is not modeled.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.note: Flat 4.95%; no standard deduction; $2,850 exemption per filer (lost above $250,000 of AGI, $500,000 joint — not modeled).

IN.name: Indiana
IN.note: Flat 3.0% state rate; $1,000 exemption per filer. County income taxes not included; Indiana has no head-of-household status.

IA.name: Iowa
IA.note: Flat 3.8% of federal taxable income, so the federal standard deduction applies. Exemption credits and the alternate tax not modeled.

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.note: Flat 4.0%. One standard deduction per joint return (spouses filing separately on a combined return each take one — not modeled). No head-of-household status. Local occupational taxes not included.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.note: Flat 3.0% (Act 11, 2024 3rd Extraordinary Session); no personal exemption.

MI.name: Michigan
MI.note: Flat 4.25%; $5,800 exemption per filer. City income taxes not included; Michigan has no head-of-household status.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.note: Flat 3.07%; no standard deduction or exemption. Pennsylvania taxes 401(k) deferrals, which the estimate subtracts; local earned income taxes not included.

UT.name: Utah
UT.note: Flat 4.5% (HB 106). The taxpayer tax credit (6% of the federal standard deduction, phased out) is not modeled.

CA.name: California
CA.note: 1%–12.3%, plus 1% on taxable income over $1,000,000 for every status. Exemption credits not modeled.

NY.name: New York
NY.note: The tax benefit recapture above NY AGI of $107,650 is not modeled. NYC and Yonkers taxes not included.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.note: No standard deduction; $1,000 exemption per filer.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.note: 5% plus the 4% surtax over $1,083,150; no standard deduction.

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.note: Standard deduction phase-out above $238,950 of AGI and the 1% net investment income tax not modeled.

OR.name: Oregon
OR.note: The subtraction for federal income tax (up to $8,500) and the exemption credit are not modeled, so the estimate runs high. Portland-area local taxes not included.

OH.name: Ohio
OH.note: No tax up to $26,050. Exemption shown for MAGI over $80,000. Joint filing credit and school district / municipal taxes not modeled.

VA.name: Virginia
VA.note: No head-of-household status (files as single). Spouse tax adjustment not modeled.

WI.name: Wisconsin
WI.note: Sliding-scale standard deduction. Head of household uses the single scale, exact above $57,210 of income. Married couple credit not modeled.

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.note: Starts from federal taxable income at pre-OBBBA standard deduction amounts. Two-wage-earner credit not modeled.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.note: County income tax (2.25%–3.30%) not included. The exemption steps down above $100,000 of AGI ($150,000 joint/head of household) and is gone above $150,000 ($200,000); modeled as a straight line.

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.note: Exemption falls $1,000 per $1,000 of AGI (modeled as a straight line). The 2% rate phase-out, tax recapture and personal tax credit tables are not modeled.

AL.name: Alabama
AL.note: Standard deduction steps down with AGI (modeled as a straight line). The deduction for federal income tax is not modeled, so the estimate runs high. Local occupational taxes not included.

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.note: One table for every status. Between $94,700 and $100,000 of net income the lower brackets are recaptured, which the estimate misses (up to about $330). Personal tax credits not modeled.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.note: One table for every status; combined-separate filing not modeled. Personal credit ($110 per person) not modeled.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.note: Standard deduction = the federal amount. The deduction for federal income tax and per-spouse tax on combined returns are not modeled. Kansas City / St. Louis earnings taxes not included.

MT.name: Montana
MT.note: Starts from federal taxable income, so the federal standard deduction applies.

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.note: Standard deduction = the federal amount; the exemption is the low- and middle-income exemption.

ND.name: North Dakota
ND.note: Starts from federal taxable income. Marriage penalty credit not modeled.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.note: Deduction and exemption phase out in 20% steps above $254,250 of AGI (straight line here).

VT.name: Vermont
VT.note: Minimum tax of 3% of AGI above $150,000 not modeled.

DC.name: District of Columbia
DC.note: DC's own standard deduction (not the higher OBBBA federal amount).

ID.name: Idaho
ID.note: 5.3% above a zero-rate band; standard deduction = the federal amount.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.note: 4.4% above $10,000 of taxable income. On a combined return each earning spouse gets a $10,000 zero band (not modeled).

2026.source_note: Federal & FICA: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 / SSA 2026. State schedules: each state's 2026 rates, deductions and exemptions by filing status, or its 2025 figures where 2026 ones are not yet published (credits and local taxes not included). Estimate only — not tax advice; verify against official sources.

capital_gains.source_note: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.03 — long-term capital gains 0%/15%/20% breakpoints by filing status.

LA.name: Louisiana

MI.name: Michigan

NY.name: New York
NY.note: The tax benefit recapture above NY AGI of $107,650 is not modeled. NYC and Yonkers taxes not included.

NJ.name: New Jersey

MA.name: Massachusetts

MN.name: Minnesota

OR.name: Oregon

OH.name: Ohio

WI.name: Wisconsin

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.note: Act 110 of 2026: starts from federal AGI; the SC Income Adjusted Deduction phases out by $95,000 of AGI ($190,000 joint, $142,500 head of household); no itemizing.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.note: County income tax (2.25%–3.30%) not included. Exemption steps down above $100,000 of AGI ($150,000 joint/head of household), modeled as a straight line. 2026 standard deduction not yet published; 2025 amounts used.

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.note: Exemption falls $1,000 per $1,000 of AGI (modeled as a straight line). The 2% rate phase-out, tax recapture and personal tax credit tables are not modeled.

AL.name: Alabama
AL.note: Standard deduction steps down with AGI (modeled as a straight line). The deduction for federal income tax is not modeled, so the estimate runs high. Local occupational taxes not included.

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.note: Top rate 3.7% (Act 1, 2026). Statutory brackets (DFA may index them) and the 2025 standard deduction; 2026 indexed figures not yet published. The recapture of the lower brackets above $94,700 of net income is not modeled. Personal tax credits not modeled.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.note: One table for every status; combined-separate filing not modeled. Personal credit ($110 per person) not modeled.

ME.name: Maine
ME.note: Includes the 2% surcharge on very high incomes from 2026.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.note: Standard deduction = the federal amount. The deduction for federal income tax and per-spouse tax on combined returns are not modeled. Kansas City / St. Louis earnings taxes not included.

MT.name: Montana
MT.note: Starts from federal taxable income, so the federal standard deduction applies (HB 337 rates).

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.note: Standard deduction = the federal amount; the exemption is the low- and middle-income exemption.

ND.name: North Dakota
ND.note: Starts from federal taxable income. Marriage penalty credit not modeled.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.note: Deduction and exemption phase out in 20% steps above $261,000 of AGI (straight line here).

VT.name: Vermont
VT.note: Preliminary 2026 brackets; 2026 standard deduction and exemption not yet published (2025 amounts used). Minimum tax of 3% of AGI above $150,000 not modeled.

DC.name: District of Columbia
DC.note: DC's own standard deduction; its 2026 inflation adjustment is not yet published (2025 amounts used).

ID.name: Idaho
ID.note: 5.3% above a zero-rate band; standard deduction = the federal amount. 2026 zero-rate band not yet published; 2025 thresholds used.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.note: 4.0% above $10,000 of taxable income. On a combined return each earning spouse gets a $10,000 zero band (not modeled).
